sentences.span: oil prices are somewhat elevated but refined product prices (and crack spreads) are near record levels... perpetuating the price difference between refined products and crude (and thus crack spreads)
sentences.why: Bernstein's note directly frames crude as headline-driven (Strait of Hormuz) while refined product/crack spreads carry the physical shortage and the two have diverged.

sentences.span: Markets seem to only react badly when actual events affecting energy prices occur. Markets seem to react positively to any story, rumor, or hope that is positive.
sentences.why: Tchir (Academy Securities) states exactly this stance on oil-price behavior around positive rumors/de-escalation stories; the pulse applies it to a ceasefire rumor, a natural instance of the stated pattern.

No JPMorgan-authored document exists anywhere in the day's source set (bank list: Academy Securities, Allianz, BTIG, Bank of America, Barclays, Bernstein, Capital Group, Deutsche Bank, Eastspring, Generali, Goldman Sachs, HSBC, Morgan Stanley, Northern Trust, One River, Other, RBC, Societe Generale, The Market Ear, UBS). The only 'fair value roughly $10-15 higher' oil call found is Goldman's Jared Cohen (GIR), not JPMorgan.

sentences.span: The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike... Fri. 18 September
sentences.why: Explicitly conditional ('if that read is right'); its only checkable anchor, that central banks hiked last week, is supported (Fed FOMC hike per 17157/17196 and BoJ hike per 17190, both in the week before this pulse).

No JPMorgan document exists in the source set, and no Bank of America document discusses being short 2-year Treasuries or a 'not restrictive enough' rates view (the three BofA-sourced files are about CPU TAM, Broadcom, and internet capex). The Trump-Xi/Thursday/Andrews AFB framing appears only in a Bear Traps ('Other') chat log, not JPMorgan, and with no '$16' figure attached.
This describes the pulse's own prior trade call from 'last Monday,' not a claim any bank research document could support; no source document in the set addresses it.

sentences.span: HYPERSCALERS: POST DISTRIBUTION FREE CASH FLOW IS NOW NEGATIVE ... UNDERPERFORMANCE OF HYPERSCALERS AND RISE IN CREDIT SPREADS
sentences.why: SG's deck shows hyperscaler FCF turning negative alongside rising credit spreads; GS's Will Wolcott (17186) independently confirms AI capex is now funded via a widening hyperscaler credit basket ('the AI theme has transitioned...to more of a credit and funding story'); GS Pasquariello (17232) ties rising energy prices directly to the 'melt higher in global bond yields,' supporting the yields linkage.

This sentence asserts a substantive counter-argument exists 'inside the same houses'; the only counter content the pulse actually offers (s9) is fabricated, and no genuine AI-overinvestment counter-narrative with comparable substance appears in the source set (only a marketing teaser headline 'AI: Bubble or boom?').

No source document mentions a BofA fund manager survey figure of 33% (or any percentage) on AI overinvestment, and none gives Goldman semiconductor gross margins at 70% against a 15-year average of 55%.

sentences.span: This would be exacerbated if the Fed were to hike in October given the >50% chance currently priced in.
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley states market pricing for an October hike is just above 50%, fairly characterized as 'a coin flip.'

Sources describe the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.7% (Generali, 17157) or 'approaching 4.75%' (MS, 17196); no document gives the precise 4.744% figure. This reads as a live market data pull rather than a sourced research figure.

sentences.span: In the US, funds sold Semis, broader AI Tech, Discretionary and Industrials / Energy exposures, while adding to Hyperscalers, Optical Networking, Cybersecurity, Financials and Materials
sentences.why: The semis-to-financials rotation is real, but the source only supports it as a single week's prime-brokerage flow (as of Thursday), not a trend running 'since the Nasdaq peaked in early June' — no document anywhere describes an early-June Nasdaq peak or a rotation of that duration.

sentences.span: Breadth has become another pretty clear indication of how much harder the tape has been than the headline index suggests. Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average.
sentences.why: GS Coppersmith documents resilient headline index concurrent with deteriorating breadth (concentration carrying the tape), which is what the sentence's checkable content describes; the 'market top' framing is interpretive gloss on real, sourced breadth data, not an invented fact.

sentences.span: BoJ Policy Rate ... 1.25% ... 1.00% ... The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike, citing rising upside inflation risks. Sato and Asada dissented in favour of no policy change
sentences.why: The rate (1.25%), the 25bp hike, and two named dissenters are all sourced. But 'highest since 1995' and the claim that both dissenters were board members appointed by PM Takaichi appear nowhere in the source set — invented embellishment on a real event.

No source gives an August core inflation print of 1.7% against a 1.8% expectation, and no document attributes a January 2027 next-move call to UBS and Goldman (the only inflation figure found in that range is 'core CPI rose 0.29%' m/m in 17198, a different metric).
